references.text: Israel was instructed not to leave Egypt empty-handed, but to take silver, gold, and clothing—the same principle of not sending a slave away empty-handed.
The law concerning the release of Hebrew slaves after six years, which forms the basis for the provision in Deuteronomy 15.
The Jubilee law regarding the release of Israelite slaves, which complements the provisions about the treatment and release of slaves.
Jeremiah reminds the people of the covenant to release Hebrew slaves, a direct reference to the law in Deuteronomy 15.
God repeats the command to release Hebrew slaves after seven years, with a direct reference to this law.
The preceding verse that establishes the context for the release of Hebrew slaves in the seventh year.
The following verse that specifies what should be given to the freed slave and the reason based on Israel's own experience in Egypt.
